newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: MEDICINE BANK SAYS H1 NET PROFIT 346,000 LITAS.
newsitem.headline: MEDICINE BANK SAYS H1 NET PROFIT 346,000 LITAS.

text.p: Lithuania's Medicine bank said on Monday that its net profit in the first half of 1997 was 346,000 litas compared to over two million litas in losses in the same period last year.
The bank said in a statement that its assets rose to 58.352 million litas at the end of June from 47.797 million litas at the start of the year.
The statement also said that its loan porfolio at the end of June rose to 38.94 million litas from 29.94 million litas at the end of 1996.
The bank said its deposits were 39.6 million litas at the end of June, an increase from 35.3 million litas at the beginning of 1997.
It said that the liquidity of the bank was 100.38 percent and its capiatal adequacy ratio stood at 29.13 percent.
Medicine Bank, which rose from the ashes of Ancorobank, posted 10.1 million litas in losses for 1996.
The bank is a closed-stock company and the spokesman for the bank, Dainius Mockevichius, told Reuters it plans to be registered as a public company at the start of 1998.
The current share capital of the bank is 23.2 million litas and its shareholders' decided on June 8 to raise it by three million litas to 26.2 million litas.
